title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes, which set up an axiomatic framework of 'ateliers'/'atlases'. An atelier is a poset of formal 'figures' F with two relations: ≤ (inclusion) and << (a strict, 'relatively compact in' or interior inclusion). Fig(L) is the atelier of all finite-family figures on a set L. Page 52 defined an atlas 𝔉, satisfying axioms At1–At8, to be 'ensembliste' (set-theoretic) when the canonical map 𝔉 → Fig(L) is an embedding. Equivalently (At ens 1): multloc(F) << multloc(G) implies F << G. Page 52 then begins Example (3): a tame ('modéré') topological space E with a simplicial triangulation M, topological or tame.

This page continues that example. Unlike Example B on p. 34, there is no affine structure. Two simplices are called compatible as in loc. cit. (their intersection is a common face). This gives a set-theoretic atlas: take F to be the closed 'multiplexes', meaning finite unions of pairwise compatible simplices, ordered by ≤. Axiom A8 holds trivially, once Σ is identified with L.

Grothendieck then remarks that compatibility of simplices is finer than compatibility of the associated set-theoretic figures. Here one demands in addition that the intersection figure be 'elementary', i.e. a single common cell or face, not just any set. 'On y reviendra par la suite.'

Conclusion paragraph: for a set-theoretic atelier (𝔉, ≤, <<), the structure can be recovered from the set L and the figures it describes, as a sub-atelier of Fig(L). This raises a classification problem: which sub-ateliers of Fig(L) arise in this way?

The next page answers it via the 'Scholie'. Giving a (quasi-)set-theoretic atelier amounts to giving a pair (L, 𝔉) with 𝔉 ⊂ Fig(L) containing all point-figures {{x}}. L is then recovered as the set of minimal nonempty elements for <<.

Purpose: building a point-set or point-free axiomatics for tame topology, i.e. the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse, in which polyhedral and simplicial structures fit as examples.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The example is only sketched: it is not verified that 'multiplexes of pairwise compatible simplices' satisfy all axioms At1–At8 apart from A8.

The remark that compatibility of simplices is strictly finer than set-theoretic compatibility signals a mismatch, so the simplicial atelier is not simply the induced sub-atelier with the induced compatibility. Grothendieck defers it ('on y reviendra').

ideas.what: Triangulated tame space without affine structure, viewed as an atlas whose figures are finite unions of pairwise face-compatible closed simplices
ideas.modern_name: simplicial complex / triangulation of a tame (o-minimal-type) space; poset of subcomplexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology; tame setting: van den Dries et al. (o-minimal triangulation)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only announces 'topologie modérée'; this formalism is unpublished

ideas.what: Compatibility of simplices (intersection is a common face) is finer than compatibility of the underlying sets
ideas.modern_name: simplicial complex condition vs. arbitrary cell families

ideas.what: A set-theoretic atelier is recovered as a sub-atelier of Fig(L); problem of characterizing which sub-ateliers occur (answered on the next page by requiring the point-figures)
ideas.modern_name: representation/concreteness theorem for abstract incidence structures, analogous to spatial locales or points as minimal elements for a way-below-type relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone-duality and locale-theory tradition (Stone, Isbell, Johnstone); domain theory (Scott) for way-below relations

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags that simplicial compatibility (intersection must be elementary) is finer than set-theoretic compatibility of figures, and promises to return to it. This points to a notion of atelier with a nontrivial compatibility structure beyond the induced one. It is part of the unpublished 'ateliers' axiomatics of tame topology, which has had no follow-up in the literature.
missed.quote: la notion de compatibilité des simplexes est plus fine que la compatibilité des figures ensemblistes associées — puisqu'ici on exige de plus que la figure intersection soit élémentaire ... On y reviendra par la suite
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It is relevant only to anyone reconstructing Grothendieck's axiomatic tame topology and comparing it with o-minimal structures or with combinatorial and point-free topology.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine worked example (simplicial complexes) inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework itself is little known, but this page contains nothing a specialist would find novel mathematically.
transcription_corrections: 'nous [?] structure affine' is probably 'nous n'avons pas de structure affine' / 'sans structure affine'.
'D'où une [?] polyédrale' is likely 'D'où un atlas ensembliste' (image: '...ensembliste, en prenant').

'F ensemble des [-polyédrales-] {+simplexe+} fermés' is likely 'F ensemble des multiplexes fermés pour ≤, et formés de simplexes deux à deux compatibles'. The crossed word resembles 'multiplexes', and 'fermés de simplexes' should read 'formés de simplexes'.
'figures polyédrales associées' is likely 'figures ensemblistes associées'.
'ie soit une polyédrale convexe' is uncertain; it plausibly reads 'ie soit un multiplexe/face commun(e)' (image ends '...ensemble commune' or similar).
'dans le cas d'une notion polyédrale' is likely 'dans le cas d'un atelier ensembliste'.
'F, F se reconstitue à partir de l'une des figures des L' is likely '𝔉 se reconstitue à partir de l'ensemble des figures de L qu'il décrit'.
'sous-notion(s)' is likely 'sous-atelier(s)' (consistent with the next page).
'd'une une L on obtient ainsi' is likely 'd'un Fig(L) on obtient ainsi'.
